sections.h2: Council Bluffs and the Loess Hills
sections.html:
Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County. Its east edge runs along the Missouri River, facing Omaha, Nebraska, and a sliver of the city lies over in Mills County. Residents numbered 62,799 in 2020 and about 62,680 in mid-2025, so the market is steady rather than booming.

The city lies in the Loess Hills, so the ground rolls and drops in a way most of Iowa does not. Slope, drainage and retaining walls are normal topics when a buyer looks at a house here. The city covers about 46 square miles at 978 feet, with Lake Manawa State Park at its southern edge and viewpoints at Fairmont Park and Kirn Park.

Because the Interstate 480 bridge ties the city to downtown Omaha, a Council Bluffs house is often compared with Omaha-area options. Think about commuters on both sides of the river when you decide how to describe the house.

Named areas include Downtown, Old Town, West End, Casino Row, Twin City, Manawa, South End, Oakland-Fairview, Madison Avenue and Huntington Avenue. Mention the one your house sits in, since buyers search by area.

The river has moved the boundaries here before. Carter Lake seceded in 1926 after a change in the river's course cut it off, and an 1881 flood severed a Missouri River channel and formed Lake Manawa. For a lot near the water, have the floodplain status and any past flooding ready before the first showing or call.

Two school districts divide the city. The Council Bluffs Community School District serves most of it, with 10 elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, Abraham Lincoln and Thomas Jefferson. The Lewis Central Community School District serves the southern part. Look up your own address before you name a district to a buyer.

Two installments make up the yearly bill, and each has its own delinquent date. Iowa Code 445.37 adds timing rules that apply to Council Bluffs owners.

SituationRule
Regular datesOctober 1 for installment one, April 1 for installment two
September 30 or March 31 on a weekendDelinquency begins on the second business day of the following month
Mailed paymentMust reach the treasurer by the last business day of the preceding month, or carry a postmark before the delinquent date
Online paymentFollows its own midnight cutoff through a county treasurer's authorized site

If you sell mid-year, the title company usually prorates the bill. Confirm what has been paid with the Pottawattamie County Treasurer first.

sections.h2: What Iowa asks of a seller
sections.html:
Sellers in Iowa describe the ground as well as the building. Under Iowa Code 558.69, a groundwater hazard statement goes to the recorder along with the declaration of value.

If the property has none of the listed conditions, you skip the separate form and the deed's first page carries a set line saying so. Without the right statement, the recorder will not accept the deed. The transfer tax under Iowa Code 428A.1 is 80 cents per $500, and it is not owed when no consideration is paid.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html:
Most Council Bluffs closings go smoothly when a few items are ready early.

  • The latest tax statement from the Pottawattamie County Treasurer, with both installments shown.
  • What you know about a well, buried tank or septic system, written down for the groundwater form.
  • The deed and any prior survey, so the title company can finish its search.
  • Tenant leases, if anyone lives in the house, and a plan for the move-out date.

Once those are in a folder, the closing date can follow your schedule. A house on a slope or near the river should also come with any drainage or flood paperwork you have.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Council Bluffs house work?
sections.html:
The process starts with a conversation about the house and ends with a signature. No one tours it on weekends, and no one waits on a mortgage underwriter.

  1. Share the address, the condition and any tenant or title issue.
  2. Review the written offer and ask about anything unclear.
  3. Accepting hands the file to a title company or attorney, who drafts the deed and the filings for the Pottawattamie County recorder.
  4. Sign at closing, and the deed is recorded.

Set the number beside what repairs and a long listing would cost you. If it falls short, decline. That carries no fee.

sections.h2: Selling a house with tenants or an inherited title
sections.html:
Some Council Bluffs sales need a little extra planning. A rented house needs a decision early: does the buyer inherit the tenant, or does the tenant leave first? Pull each lease and, if the tenant is leaving, agree on the date in writing so closing can be scheduled around it.

With an inherited house, whoever signs at closing must be the person named on the deed. If the heirs are not on title yet, begin that work before collecting offers, since the title company will insist on it. No lender has to approve any of this on a cash deal, so the wait shrinks once the papers are right.

Say plainly if the house needs work you do not want to manage. The offer is built on the condition you describe, and the decision stays yours.

Closing is mostly signing. The title company brings the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement, or the deed line that replaces it, and you sign where marked. The deed is then recorded in Pottawattamie County. Any property tax share you owe is paid from the sale money, and so is any loan balance still sitting on the house.

Before that day, call the Pottawattamie County Treasurer for a payoff on any unpaid installment, schedule final utility readings and clear the house of anything you are keeping. Bring identification and keys, and ask the title company how and when the proceeds reach you. Knowing the answer to that last question ahead of time keeps the day calm.

sections.h2: Describing a hillside or riverside house
sections.html:
Terrain is part of what a Council Bluffs buyer is paying for. A lot in the bluffs may have steep grades, stairs, retaining walls or a drive that is hard in winter, and a buyer who learns that late tends to lower the offer. Mention each one when you first talk, along with anything you have done about erosion or runoff.

For a house nearer the river or Lake Manawa, the questions turn to water. Collect any insurance paperwork, repair receipts and notes on a wet basement. Honest, specific answers make an offer easier to give and easier to trust, and they cut down on surprises between acceptance and closing.

faqs.q: Is Council Bluffs the county seat of Pottawattamie County?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the county seat, and a small piece of the city extends into Mills County.

faqs.q: How many people live in Council Bluffs?
faqs.a: Residents numbered 62,799 in 2020 and about 62,680 in mid-2025, so the market is steady rather than booming.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Council Bluffs house in?
faqs.a: The Council Bluffs Community School District covers most addresses. Southern addresses fall in Lewis Central Community Schools.

faqs.q: When did Council Bluffs get its name?
faqs.a: The town was called Kanesville until about 1852 or 1853 and was incorporated as Council Bluffs on January 19, 1853. The name goes back to an 1804 meeting between Lewis and Clark and the Otoe.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: October 1 starts delinquency on the first installment, and April 1 does so for the second. When the day before is a weekend, the date shifts to the second business day of that month.
